maya: quick summary from the night nsys vs sampling runs on a p4 cluster — results and proposed guardrails

maya: tl;dr: full nsys traces add ~18-22% median latency and ~600-800MB RAM; lightweight sampling (1/50 requests + nvtx markers) shows ~2.1-2.8% median overhead and <50MB extra memory. detailed stats and artifacts attached. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sam: solid. can you drop the run ids + artifact link?

maya: perfbot uploaded the artifacts: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/1768500000-sample-vs-full.zip

maya: commands used for reference:
```
# full capture
nsys profile --output full_seq128_kv_on --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none ./run_inference.sh --seq 128 --kv-cache on

# lightweight sampling harness (runtime uses nvtx markers)
profiler --mode=sample --rate=0.02 --markers=nvtx ./run_inference.sh --seq 128 --kv-cache on
```

jonathan: a couple of observations from the timelines: full traces show many small memcpy + cuLaunch kernel events that blow up scheduling overheads; when seq_len increases the overhead fraction goes up because kernels run longer and profiler hooks add cumulative overhead.

eli: interesting — how does KV cache hit rate affect the numbers? my worry is sampling missing cache-cold flows that drive perf regressions.

maya: good point. we correlated traces with kv hit/miss tags (we instrumented nvtx push/pop around cache lookup). results: when kv hit rate >= 90% the relative overhead of sampling drops (fewer kernels on hot paths), but full nsys still shows the same absolute overhead due to traced host-side events. for cache-cold runs the sampling overhead was slightly higher (~3.8%) because sampled traces capture longer traces and more kernel transitions.

sam: sounds like naive uniform sampling might miss noisy cold path regressions. what heuristics do we want?

jonathan: proposal: hybrid sampling rule — prioritize sampling on requests that either (a) miss the KV cache, (b) exceed runtime latency threshold (e.g., > p95 baseline), or (c) are random at low base rate. put it together with a global token-bucket to cap traces per shard.

eli: +1. also add a backoff if we detect profiler-induced tail increases. in our tests full capture caused a transient p99 spike; we should fail-safe to stop profiling automatically.

maya: proposed guardrails to implement in runtime:
- default mode: "sample" (not full). default rate: 0.005 (0.5%).
- extra trigger: always sample if kv_cache_miss == true (configurable).
- token bucket per-worker: max_traces_per_minute = 6 (configurable).
- disable full-mode in prod unless explicitly allowed by an opt-in flag and under a maintenance window.
- automatic backoff: if p50 latency increases by >5% or p95 by >10% during profiling window, throttle to zero and emit alert to #eng-runtime.

maya: runtime config snippet for the initial PR:
```
profiler:
  mode: "sample"            # sample | full | off
  base_rate: 0.005           # fraction of random requests
  kv_miss_force: true        # sample on cache miss
  max_traces_per_min: 6
  safe_full_enabled: false
```

sam: good. what about correlation ids and privacy? we need traces to include session_id and route metadata so we can map to eval prompt sets, but strip PII.

maya: yes — sampled traces will include request_id, route, seq_len, kv_hit boolean, and an anonymized session token; no raw prompt text in prod. full captures in staging can include more.

jonathan: implementation notes: add NVTX markers around the KV lookup and critical runtime state transitions. add a cheap per-request check at ingress that decides to attach profiler token to the request. ensure the profiler path doesn't allocate large buffers on the hot path (avoid extra allocations).

maya: measured overhead numbers (summary):
- full nsys (seq=128, kv on): median latency +20% (range 18-22%), mem +700MB, run timeouts observed at 1/200 runs
- sample 1/50 (seq=128, kv on): median +2.4% (range 2.1-2.8%), mem +30-40MB
- sample 1/200 with kv_miss_force: median +1.1%, but catch rate for cold-path regressions ~76% in our sim

eli: can we make the sampling rate adaptive? e.g., increase rate if we detect new regression signals.

sam: yes — use a local controller that increases sample rate for N minutes when it sees a spike in error/latency and decays back. controlled by policy in console.

maya: runbook (first cut):
1) enable mode=sample, base_rate=0.005, kv_miss_force=true on canary region for 24h.
2) monitor p50/p90/p99; if tail > baseline+10% revert and notify.
3) if we need deeper info, run full capture in staging or run a limited full capture in prod with safe_full_enabled=true and only for 1 shard with admin approval.

perfbot: artifact uploaded: s3://perf-artifacts/1768500000-sample-vs-full.zip :thumbsup:

sam: ok. action items — maya to open PR for runtime token-bucket + config + nvtx markers; jonathan to run a 24h canary with new defaults and report; eli to draft the runbook and alert thresholds. i'll add a quick dashboard with profiler-on vs profiler-off buckets.

maya: i'll tag the PR and add test vectors (seq 32/128/512) + kv hit/miss cases. aiming for small PR by EOD.

jonathan: one more caveat — make sure we don't sample too aggressively for very short requests (<5ms) because relative overhead noise is larger. maybe exclude requests below a latency floor.

maya: good call. add min_request_ms = 3 to config.

sam: thanks all. solid plan. :rocket:
